prosody.lang: Walk down a marble street; at the end, a two thousand year old library is waiting. Enter by the upper gate and walk downhill. The marble under your feet has taken so many steps over the centuries that it shines. Merchants and philosophers once walked here. Ephesus was a harbour city. Ships sailed almost into town. Then, year after year, the

River carried down silt and filled the harbour. Today the sea is kilometres away. Slow down on Curetes Street. On your right is the arch of the Temple of Hadrian, with a face in its centre watching you. Further on are the Terrace Houses, with mosaics and frescoes. And at the end of the street the facade appears: the Library of Celsus. Two storeys of columns, raised up again. A son built it for his father, as a tomb and a library at once. Sit on the library steps and look back up the street. Then walk to the Great Theatre and climb to the top row. Say one word out loud, and hear it carry across seats that once held twenty thousand people.
